questions.question: Which one of the following landforms is/are formed by wind erosion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zeugen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zeugens **are elongated, resistant ridges or hills of rock that remain after surrounding areas have been eroded by wind or water.

 
 
• They are often found in arid or semi-arid regions where **wind erosion is a significant geomorphic process**.
 
• Mostly seen in arid and **semi-arid areas**.
 
• The **soft part of the rock** is destroyed by the wind and the hard part remains the same.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cirque** is a landform associated with **glacial erosion**. Cirques are amphitheater-shaped valleys with precipitous walls.
 
• **Stack **is typically formed by **coastal erosion**.
 
 
• Generally seen in coastal areas.
 
• The formation of Stacks takes a very long time.

questions.question: Which type of soil is formed due to the deposition of sediments by rivers such as the Gandak, Burhi Gandak, Mahananda, Kosi,?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of the above**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The deposition of sediments by these rivers contributes to the formation of Piedmont Swamp Soil, Terai Soil, and Gangetic Alluvium Soil in the Northern Plain of Bihar.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** 

The state of Bihar is situated on the World's most fertile alluvial plain of Gangetic Valley 

 
• Piedmont Swamp Soil: This soil is swallowing too deep over bedrocks and pebbles. Swamp soil is mostly clayey, rich in organic matter and neutral reaction. This is mostly found in the Northwestern Champaran district.
 
• Terai Soil: Terai soil is grey to yellow and neutral to moderately acidic in reaction. The soil of lowland Terai is more fertile than upland terai. This is mostly found in the northern part of Bihar nearby the border of Nepal and the foothill of the Himalayas.
 
• Gangetic Alluvium Soil: It is generally fertile in Bihar plain but regular tillage without application of manure has costs low organic content. Gangetic alluvium soil is mostly loamy with varying thickness. It is thicker towards the north and thinner towards the south.
 
• Karail-Kewal Soil: This is heavy clay soil (alkaline feature). This soil is found in Rohtas to Gaya, Aurangabad, Jahanabad, Munger, and Bhagalpur. This soil is best suited for rice and rabi crops like wheat, linseed, pulses, and gram.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements (A) and (B) about destruction of forests in Amazon basin and choose the appropriate option.

**Statement (A) :** The topsoil is being washed away by rain fall and the lush forest is turning into a barren landscape.

**Statement (B) :** A large area of rain forest in amazon basin has been disappearing due to developmental activities.
questions.solution:
Both (A) and (B) are correct

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

**Statement (A): The topsoil is being washed away by rainfall and the lush forest is turning into a barren landscape.**

 
• This is true.
 
• Deforestation in the Amazon Basin has led to the loss of the topsoil, which is the most fertile part of the soil and vital for plant growth.
 
• When the forest is removed, the soil is exposed to the elements, including heavy rainfall typical of the region.
 
• Without trees and plants to help hold the soil together with their root systems, the rain can easily wash the soil away, leading to a process known as soil erosion.
 
• This erosion can change the fertile landscape into a barren, unproductive one.

**Statement (B): A large area of rain forest in the Amazon Basin has been disappearing due to developmental activities.**

 
• This is also true.
 
• The Amazon rainforest has been significantly impacted by human activities, particularly due to development such as logging, agriculture (including the creation of pastures for livestock), mining, and the construction of dams and roads.
 
• These activities lead to deforestation, which is the permanent removal of trees to make room for something besides the forest.
 
• This has resulted in a significant loss of forest area in the Amazon Basin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**The question asks to match different types of forests with their corresponding regions.

__
 
• **Option 1 (A)-(i), (B)-(iii), (C)-(iv), (D)-(ii) is incorrect** because it matches **Tropical Deciduous with regions close to the Equator and Tropics,** which is actually the characteristic of Tropical Evergreen forests.
 
• Similarly, it matches Temperate Deciduous with North Eastern USA, China, New Zealand, and Chile, which is characteristic of Temperate Evergreen forests.
 
• **Option 2** (A)-(iii), (B)-(i), (C)-(ii), (D)-(iv) is the correct answer because it matches the correct forest types with their corresponding regions.
 
• **Tropical Deciduous forests** are found in** India, Northern Australia, and Central America,** while **Tropical Evergreen forests **are found in** South East USA, South China, and East Brazil.** **Temperate Evergreen forests** are found in regions close to the poles, such as** Canada, Alaska, and Russia, **while Temperate Deciduous forests are found in regions with moderate climates, such a**s North Eastern USA and China.**
 
• **Option 3 (A)-(i), (B)-(ii), (C)-(iv), (D)-(iii) is incorrect** because it matches Tropical Deciduous with regions close to the Equator and Tropics, which is actually the characteristic of Tropical Evergreen forests.
 
• **Option 4 (A)-(ii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(iii), (D)-(ii) is incorrect **because it matches Tropical Deciduous with regions close to the poles, which is characteristic of Temperate Evergreen forests. Option 5 does not provide any answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Tropical Deciduous forests **are characterized by a** distinct dry season** and are found in regions with **monsoon climates.**
 
• **Tropical Evergreen forests** are characterized by **high rainfall** and are found in regions with **humid tropical climates.**
 
• **Temperate Evergreen forests** are characterized by coniferous trees and are found in regions with **cold climates.**
 
• **Temperate Deciduous forests **are characterized by trees that lose their leaves in the winter and are found in** regions with moderate climates.**

questions.question: Which of the following statement is true?

options.text: Tropical evergreen forests are the monsoon forests.
Tropical evergreen forests are found in the regions near the equator and close to the tropics.
Trees in tropical evergreen forests shed their leaves in the dry season.
Sal, Teak and Neem are examples of trees found in tropical evergreen forests.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is Tropical evergreen forests are found in the regions near the equator and close to the tropics.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

**Tropical evergreen forests, also known as rainforests, are primarily located in regions near the equator. **

__
 
• **T**hese areas receive high annual rainfall and have consistently warm temperatures, making them ideal for the growth of lush, diverse vegetation.
 
• The equatorial belt, which extends about 10 to 15 degrees north and south of the equator, houses most of these forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Tropical evergreen forests are not the same as monsoon forests.
 
• Monsoon forests, also known as tropical deciduous forests, are different in that they have a distinct dry season, during which trees may shed their leaves to conserve water.
 
• In tropical evergreen forests, trees retain their leaves year-round because these regions do not have a dry season.

**Sal, teak, and neem are typical of deciduous forests, not evergreen forests. Evergreen forests include trees like mahogany, ebony, and rosewood.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding Tropical Rain forests?

1. Presence of Epiphytes

2. High fertile soil

3. Reduced Wind pollination

4. Dark green coloured leaves in the lower region

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 3 and 4 only.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Tropical Rain forests:**

 
• **High temperatures and abundant rainfall **support a luxuriant tropical rainforest.
 
• In the Amazon lowlands, the **forest is so dense that it is called ‘Selvas’.**
 
• Unlike the temperate regions, the growing season here is all the **year round-seeding, flowering, fruiting and decaying do not take place in a seasonal pattern.**
 
• The equatorial vegetation comprises a multitude of evergreen trees that **yield tropical hardwood**, **e.g. mahogany, ebony, dyewoods etc.**
 
• Many parts of the tropical rainforests have been **cleared either for lumbering or shifting cultivation.**
 
• From the air, the **tropical rainforest appears like a thick canopy of foliage,** broken only where it is crossed by large rivers or cleared for cultivation.
 
• **All plants struggle upwards (most epiphytes)** for sunlight resulting in a peculiar layer arrangement.
 
• An **Epiphyte **is a plant that grows harmlessly upon another plant (such as a tree) and derives its moisture and nutrients from the air, rain, and sometimes from debris accumulating around it. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **The fertility of topsoil in rainforest regions is very poor. **
 
• Torrential downpours wash out most of the topsoil nutrients.
 
• The **soil deteriorates rapidly **with subsequent soil erosion and soil impoverishment.
 
• **It takes decades to replenish the soil with lost nutrients. ***Hence, statement 2 is not correct.*
 
• **Wind pollination**, though common in temperate regions, is assumed to be **rare or absent in Tropical Rain forests.** 
 
• It is because the **wind is an inefficient carrier of pollen in species-rich tropical communities** where conspecific individuals are usually widely spaced. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• **Rainforest plants tend to have dark green leaves**, and this relates directly to the amount of light they can absorb.
 
• Black (or dark) objects absorb all light while white (or lightly coloured) objects reflect light. Therefore, darker leaves absorb more light. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*

• Corrosion, in the context of geological processes, involves the chemical weathering and dissolution of rock, especially limestone, due to the action of acidic waters. 
 
• This type of erosion is commonly seen in karst landscapes where the dissolution of carbonate rock (such as limestone) by slightly acidic water (containing carbonic acid from dissolved CO2 in rainwater) creates features like caves, sinkholes, and underground streams. 
 
• The term "corrosion" aptly describes this process of material being gradually worn away by chemical action, distinguishing it from mechanical processes such as abrasion (physical wearing down of rocks by friction and impact) or cavitation (formation of vapor cavities in a liquid). 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 4, Corrosion.**

Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

 
 

 
 
**List I**

 
**(Soil type)**

 
 
 
**List II**

 
**(Characteristics)**

 
 
 

 A. Vertisols
 1. Soils of grasslands in sub-humid to semiarid climates
 
 

 B. Mollisols
 2. Rich in clay content and highly basic
 
 

 C. Alfisols
 3. Poor soils in terms of agricultural productivity
 
 

 D. Spodosols
 4. Clay-rich horizon produced by illuviation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**US Department of Agriculture (USDA) Soil Taxonomy:**

 
• In recent years, the US Department of Agriculture has adopted a system of soil classification based on observed soil properties rather than genetic considerations.
 
• There are twelve (12) orders of soils, which are distinguished largely on the basis of properties that reflect a major course of development, with considerable emphasis on the presence or absence of notable diagnostic horizons.

**Alfisols:**

 
• The Alfisols are soils characterized by a **clay-rich horizon produced by illuviation and high base status.**
 
• The world distribution of Alfisols is **extremely wide in latitude**, ranging from as high as 60° N in North America and Eurasia to the equatorial zone in South America and Africa Because the Alfisols span an enormous range in climate types, four important suborders of Alf sols, each with its own climate affiliation.

**Spodosols:**

 
• Spodosols have a **light-colored albic horizon of eluviation, and a dense spodic horizon of illuviation.**
 
• They develop under cold needle-leaf forests and are quite acidic. Spodosols are closely associated with regions recently covered by the great ice sheets of the Late Cenozoic Ice Age.
 
• Spodosols are **naturally poor soils in terms of agricultural productivity.** Because they are** acidic, lime application is essential.**

**Vertisols:**

 
• Vertisols **develop on certain types of volcanic rock in wet-dry climates under grassland and savanna vegetation.**
 
• They expand and contract with wetting and drying, creating deep cracks in the soil.
 
• They are** black in color and have a high content of the clay mineral montmorillonite**, which is formed from the weathering of particular volcanic rocks.
 
• An important region of Vertisols is the **Deccan Plateau of western India**, where basalt, a dark variety of igneous rock, supplies the silicate minerals that are altered into the necessary clay minerals.

**Mollisols:**

 
• Mollisols are soils of** grasslands in sub-humid to semiarid climates.**
 
• They have a** thick, dark brown surface layer, termed a mollic epipedon.**
 
• Because of their loose texture and high base status, they are **highly productive.**
 
• In North America, Mollisols dominate the Great Plains region, the Columbia Plateau, and the northern Great Basin. In South America, a large area of Mollisols covers the Pampa region of Argentina and Uruguay.
 
• In Eurasia, a great belt of Mollisols stretches from Romania eastward across the steppes of Russia, Siberia, and Mongolia.
